title: P4RPC: Decode "haveRec" fields, display time as ISO-8601 strings:
description:
- Bump internal version to 1.0.6
- Decode "haveRec" fields (structs)
- All time fields are now displayed as ISO-8601 strings.
- Add functions to convert "seconds" integer or string to ISO-8601 format strings.
- Add preference to display time fields as UTC or local time zone.
- Time formatting functions allow the precision to be specified.
- Compute time strings only once per time field.
- Flag datetimes that are not set.
- Don't add the haveRec subfields if we aren't displaying var=val as a subtree.
- Allow filtering on "p4rpc.synctime" and "p4rpc.synctime.val".
- Change "hide_nul" pref to "show_nul".
- Update descriptions of remaining "p4rpc.\*" variables.
- Rename "p4rpc.cksum.len" to "p4rpc.len.cksum".
- Ensure that snprintf bufs are terminated.
- Improve some comments.

created #21013 to continue this discussion
Why add a FT_STRING and a FT_UINT64 field instead of adding a FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME if you want to be able to filter and compare?

Three reasons:

1. I want to format it as ISO-8601 rather than "DoW Mon Day Time..."
2. I want to display it in either UTC or localtime, depending on a preference setting.
3. More importantly, although it's normally 4 bytes the protocol allows it to be 8 bytes.  Does FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME support  8-byte timestamps?  I used FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME at first but changed the code when I thought that it didn't.

I'll look more closely at the FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME implementation -- maybe it supports all three and I missed that when I read the code.  Obviously it's preferable to use FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME if I can.

I see that FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME supports several timestamp sizes of **binary** data. This "syncTime" is not binary -- it's an ASCII decimal **string** of the timestamp, so FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME isn't usable. I removed the FT_STRING tree var because it's redundant (the string tree var was already added), but the FT_UINT64 tree var is needed in order to support integer comparisons rather than just string comparisons).

FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME also supports several ways to encoding time as strings, though not currently strings that are just seconds since an epoch. You also can convert a string to an `nstime_t` and then add it to a FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME field using `proto_tree_add_item` (and `proto_tree_add_item_format_value`, etc.)

You should be able to use the function `unix_epoch_to_nstime` to generate an nstime_t to manipulate and add to the tree.

(In fact, tvb_get_string_time() should probably support ENC_TIME_SECS and similar, so that eventually `proto_tree_add_time_item` could be used.)
I'll take a look; that would be better than re-implementing this functionality.

I've gone back and forth about this.  There's a lot of useful info from the TCP layer (although I don't normally find the TSval and TSecr fields very helpful), and it's not uncommon for P4RPC packets to contain dozens of messages and therefore '_func_'s would run off the end of the INFO line -- and it's not easy to pick out the "interesting" '_func_'s in a long horizontal list.  I found it more useful to show the number of messages, leave the TCP info, and look at the Details pane to see an easier-to-read vertical list of '_func_'s.

I could add a preference option to clear the INFO column then add the '_func_'s and the message count rather than just append the message count -- do you think that would be useful?  Maybe "Replace lower-level (TLS or TCP) fields in the INFO column by P4RPC message func names"

It's really whatever you and others will find most useful, but when I configured the port for p4rpc I initially thought it wasn't working (as I could still see the TCP information, and didn't spot what you appended to the end).

My personal taste would be to have it say something minimal like:

client-CloseFile | client-Ack | flush1

I'll try that and see how it feels.  In the past I've used

`[client-CloseFile] [client-Ack] [flush1]`

but I'll try your format; it's a little cleaner.  I'll add a pref because there are definitely times when I want to see the TCP info in the INFO column.
Yours is simpler, in the sense that you don't need to be aware of whether first or last in list...
True, but that's easily handled (but it is the reason that I originally used the bracket format).

Is this close to what you want? I moved the message count to the beginning of the INFO column so that it is visible even with a lot of messages in a frame, and it also provides a visual separation from the preceding columns.

![wireshark-p4rpc_2026-02-10_21-21-16.png](/uploads/b5591a375681a3367d468239f7ac7eea/wireshark-p4rpc_2026-02-10_21-21-16.png){width="900" height="233"}

Thanks for the suggestion -- I added a preference to switch between this display and my previous one, and made this the default. There are times when I want to see the TCP info but I think that you're correct -- this is more useful most of the time.

I'm planning to push this change when I resolve the issue below about `sizeof(uint32_t)`, but I can push it now if you'd like to try it out.

UPDATE: I went ahead and pushed this change but I didn't squash first, so I've cancelled the pipeline. After I have resolved Alexis's issue (`sizeof`) I'll squash and push again so that it'll be ready to commit if it passes review.

And here's the modified preference pane.

![image.png](/uploads/9557227fec1332724e68d463039a06cc/image.png){width=900 height=372}

That looks really good to me, Mark.  I suspect that when you need to look at TCP, you'll find that sequence analysis / expert info / custom columns are more useful to you than what TCP writes to the Info column.
can you replace sizeof by directly size ?

I don't think that I understand what you mean by _directly size_ -- do you mean to use a literal `4`?  The file rev number (and file type) are always `uint32_t` and `sizeof(uint32_t)` is a compile-time constant so there's no overhead to using it instead of `4`, and `sizeof(uint32_t)` expresses intent much more clearly.

Am I misunderstanding you?
The common form in most dissectors is to give the number of bytes read from the tvb.

I still don't understand; sorry to be so dense.  Aren't we talking about lines 326-327 here?

```c
proto_tree_add_item( have_tree, hf_p4rpc_have_file_rev, tvb, cur_offset,
    sizeof(uint32_t), ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN );
```

Are either of you suggesting changing them to this?

```c
proto_tree_add_item( have_tree, hf_p4rpc_have_file_rev, tvb, cur_offset,
     4, ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN );
```

This code is adding the 4 bytes at `cur_offset` to the tree, so `sizeof(uint32_t)` **is** the number of bytes we're getting from the `tvb`.

I clearly don't understand what change you're suggesting, sorry.  Am I looking at the wrong line of code?
no like Anders say, it is the number of bytes read on tvb and we prefer to don't use sizeof(xxx), more easy for code maintenance

So I should change lines 326-327 to this, correct?

```c
proto_tree_add_item( have_tree, hf_p4rpc_have_file_rev, tvb, cur_offset,
     4, ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN );
```

And make a similar change for each of the other uses of `sizeof(uintNN_t)` to the appropriate numeric literal as well, right?
Yes !

Thanks, Martin.

I'm not thrilled about the low-level string handling either, and I agree that it would be nice to have an API that limits the number of bytes copied (while truncating on a UTF-8 character boundary).  This code was simpler until a review pointed out that my previous code could truncate in the middle of a UTF-8 character, and suggested using `ws_utf8_truncate()` to truncate properly.  An alternative would be to use a buffer of length `ITEM_LABEL_LENGTH` (eg, 240) and let `proto_item_set_text()` truncate it, but that's pretty long for a label to be useful; in addition, on truncation `proto_item_set_text()` calls `memmove()` to insert ellipses at the beginning of the string, which seems a bit wasteful.

I wrote a workaround to truncate properly and insert ellipses at the beginning without needing to shift the string out of the way, but that's even messier low-level string manipulation.  I'm happy to leave it the way it is or to change it either to letting `proto_item_set_text()` truncate it or to post my non-`memmove()` attempt if you want to look at it.  It might be best to commit this version and then explore these two alternatives in a separate MR, if you think that they might be worthwhile.

I'm also not thrilled with my timestamp-handling code; it would be much cleaner if I could use some flavor of `FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME` for a string of digits, and if for both digit-strings and binary timestamps there was a display type similar to `ABSOLUTE_TIME_UTC` that supported formatting as an ISO-8601 timestamp string rather than as the `ABSOLUTE_TIME_UTC`  or `ABSOLUTE_TIME_DOY_UTC`, etc, formats.
